name: The Old Observatory
hours: Disused; the astronomy club holds the key and meets on clear Wednesday nights (until the curfew).
sight: A small copper-green dome on the hill north-west of campus, reached by a path through wind-bent pines. Inside, a brass refractor older than the Academy points through a slit that no longer quite closes; star charts curl on the walls and a chalkboard still carries somebody's orbit sums. It is cold, dusty and wonderful. At night the slit is a blade of stars.
things: Look through the big refractor on a club night
Read the observing log, kept in many hands for decades
Crank the dome round by its iron wheel
Find the plantation-era survey marks in the stone floor
Come up alone to think; the path is the quietest place within reach of campus
Watch the north ridge from the catwalk — Umbra House is a dark shape with no lamps
On a moonless night, look for the faint glow over the far side of the mountain
secret: Stargazing night Day 24 plants the astronomy club (upper-year members, and Dmitri Volkov from Bungalow 6, who joined for the hours) two days before the bang. The observing log has the best timestamped record of the event: Dmitri photographed a green-white streak at 02:10 on the night of Day 26 that slows before impact — it did not fall, it landed. Pippa develops the plate. The catwalk is the safest vantage on Umbra House and the place Viktor watches it from. From D27 a faint green light is visible over the north slope on moonless nights until the cordon lamps drown it.
access: Kept locked; the astronomy club meets Wednesdays. The latch can be lifted with a card — a sleeved one.
